S073-01.notes: Relative-clause subject is 'research' (singular) and the narrative is past: 'whose research ... helped make'. A 'help' and B 'have helped' are plural forms that would need a plural subject (trap: 'plasma' is the nearest noun, but plural agreement errors come from misreading); D 'helping' leaves the relative clause without a finite verb.

S073-02.notes: Complex list whose items contain internal commas, separated by semicolons ('...to stun prey; and ...'). The first item must also end with a semicolon. A comma (A) blurs item boundaries; colon (B) is not a list-item separator here; no punctuation (C) runs items together.

S073-03.notes: Subject 'The spray' is singular; present tense matches 'can aim'. B/D plural; D also past tense; C 'being' leaves no main verb.

S073-04.notes: Two independent clauses joined by the conjunctive adverb 'as a result': need semicolon before and comma after. A and D are comma splices; C is a run-on.

S073-05.notes: Parallel series of present-tense verbs with subject 'Ants': carry, feed, and then discard. A participle, B past tense, C infinitive break parallelism.

flags.note: Antecedent of 'that' is ambiguous: it can attach to 'colonies' (plural -> 'live') or to the nearer 'a bacterium, Vibrio fischeri' (singular -> 'lives'). Both readings are grammatical and factually true (V. fischeri does live inside the light organ), so A 'lives' is as defensible as C 'live' (B 'has lived' is also a grammatical singular reading). Rewrite so the relative clause attaches unambiguously, e.g. 'colonies of the bacterium Vibrio fischeri that ______' still ambiguous; better: 'colonies of bacteria (Vibrio fischeri), which ______ inside...' or make subject-verb agreement a main-clause subject.

S073-06.notes: Likely intended key C (agreement with 'colonies' across intervening phrase), but A is defensible by attaching the clause to 'a bacterium, Vibrio fischeri'. D 'living' would need no 'that'.

S073-07.notes: Pronoun stands for 'round trip' (singular) in a comparison: 'longer than that of any other animal'. B/D plural; C 'it of any other animal' is ungrammatical.

S073-08.notes: Pronoun is the object of 'regarded' (many young artists regarded her as their mentor): 'whom'. A is subject case; B 'which' not for people; C 'whose' needs a following noun.

S073-09.notes: Subject 'sales' is plural (trap: 'sheet music'); past context. A singular; C singular and wrong tense; D no finite verb.

S073-10.notes: Indirect (reported) question ends with a period. A wrongly uses a question mark; B adds an unopened closing quotation mark; D a comma cannot end the sentence/text.

S073-11.notes: After the colon, the evidence shows she depicted flaws without softening: portraits are rarely idealized. A 'rarely candid' contradicts; C 'rarely personal' contradicts the intimate content; D symbolism is not addressed.

S073-12.notes: 'Most earlier artists ... instead' signals departure from convention. B and C say the opposite; D unsupported.

S073-13.notes: Darwin's prediction, doubts, 1903 confirmation. A says disproved; B only one orchid; D no feeding explanation or 'entirely' argument.

S073-14.notes: Wright says people 'also' played a role and 'sped up the drying that was already under way', accepting orbital causation. A, B ('sole cause'), C (stronger monsoons) contradict Text 2.

S073-15.notes: She began signing as collector interest grew, so her signature carried market value; signing others' pots suggests it increased their value to collectors. B attributes an unsupported self-serving motive; C not suggested; D unsupported (no evidence those potters couldn't make the ware).

S073-16.notes: Verified: 0 mo -> 6, 2 mo -> 18, 5 mo -> 42; monotonic increase matches claim. A and C each give one area only, not a trend; D is background, not data.

S073-17.notes: Hypothesis is about mechanism (shade). Artificial shade matching nurse-plant survival isolates shade as the main benefit. D shows nurse plants help but not why (tempting trap); A and B irrelevant to young-saguaro survival via shade.

S073-18.notes: Dominance and privileges contrasted with fading power. A causal, B and C additive are illogical.

S073-19.notes: Applying each color across all panels causes visual unity. A contrast, C example, D simultaneity do not fit.

S073-20.notes: Only C pairs the 1965 proposal with the 1999 award. A omits Pulitzer; B omits the original proposal; D measures from the composition date, not the proposal (35-year arithmetic is correct but irrelevant).

S073-21.notes: C states the finding, defines Cepheids for an unfamiliar audience, and gives its significance (measuring distances). A and B lack significance (B also no definition); D is about Hubble, not Leavitt's discovery.
